extracted.intended_audience: CILIP members (children's librarians), authors, illustrators, publishers and other entrants to the Carnegie and Kate Greenaway Medals
extracted.subtask_description: Official awards process and judging criteria for the CILIP Carnegie Medal (literary) and Kate Greenaway Medal (artistic), plus the Amnesty CILIP Honour. Includes nomination/eligibility rules, panel composition, timelines, and detailed evaluative questions for literary and illustrated children's books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominations process and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominations for the next year's book awards are submitted September−October each year by members of CILIP. Nominations are checked and verified for their eligibility before nominations are announced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process is organised by the Youth Libraries Group (YLG). Nominations were announced (example) 06 November; nominations opened 1 September and ran to 06 October in the 2018 cycle. Verified nominations are published on the Press Desk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may nominate
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominations are made by members of CILIP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each member can nominate up to 2 books for the Carnegie Medal and up to 2 books for the Kate Greenaway Medal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination limits per member
rubrics_metrics.description: Each CILIP member may nominate up to two books for the Carnegie Medal and up to two books for the Kate Greenaway Medal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominations are subject to verification for eligibility before being announced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging panel composition
rubrics_metrics.description: 12 children's librarians — members of CILIP's Youth Libraries Group — form the panel of judges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel members read and assess all nominated books based on the official judging criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection stages, longlist/shortlist sizes and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: The judging panel meet to decide the longlist and shortlist for each medal and finally select the winners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longlists: 20 for Carnegie and 20 for Kate Greenaway; Shortlists: up to 8 books for each medal. Longlists are published in February, shortlists in March, and winners announced at a ceremony in June. Amnesty's judging panel chooses a title and recipient from each shortlist to receive the Amnesty CILIP Honour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — publication date window
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible the title must have been first published in the UK between 1 September and 31 August of the previous calendar year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — foreign-first publications / co-publication timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Books first published in another country must have been co-published in the UK within three months of the original publication date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — language and target audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The book must be written in the English language (either as an original work in English or a first English translation of a foreign-language work) and specifically published for children and young people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — authorship and anthologies
rubrics_metrics.description: The book may be co-authored; however, multiple author anthologies are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — e-books and previously published short pieces
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of e-books and short stories or poetry previously published in a magazine or elsewhere, the point of publication should be considered as the date when the work is published as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least 75% of the complete work must be original material published for the first time within the specified time frame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — formats and subject categories
rubrics_metrics.description: All categories of books, including poetry, non-fiction and graphic novels, in print or ebook format, for children and young people are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books by previous CILIP Carnegie and/or CILIP Kate Greenaway Medal winners are eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carnegie Medal — Overall literary quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The book that wins the Carnegie Medal should be a book of outstanding literary quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The whole work should provide pleasure, not merely from the surface enjoyment of a good read, but also the deeper subconscious satisfaction of having gone through a vicarious, but at the time of reading, a real experience that is retained afterwards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carnegie — Style
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the style or styles are appropriate to the subject and theme and conducive to the establishment of voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether dialogue and narrative work effectively together; effectiveness of literary techniques and conventions; use of language in creating narrative tension, conveying setting, atmosphere, characters, action and appropriateness to theme; where rhyme or rhythm are used, whether their use is accomplished and imaginative; and where factual information is presented, whether it is accurate and clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carnegie — The plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate construction and acceptability of the plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Is it well-constructed? Do events happen, not necessarily logically, but acceptably within the limits set by the theme? Is the final resolution of the plot credible in relation to the rest of the book?

rubrics_metrics.name: Carnegie — Characterisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the development and believability of characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Are the characters believable and convincing? Are they well-rounded and do they develop during the course of the book? Do they interact convincingly? Are characters' behaviour and patterns of speech consistent with their known background and environment? Do they act consistently in character throughout the book? How effectively are characters revealed through narration, dialogue, action, inner dialogue and through the thoughts, reactions and responses of others?

rubrics_metrics.name: Kate Greenaway Medal — Overall artistic quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The book that wins the Kate Greenaway Medal should be a book of outstanding artistic quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The whole work should provide pleasure from a stimulating and satisfying visual experience which leaves a lasting impression. Illustrated work needs to be considered primarily in terms of its graphic elements, and where text exists particular attention should be paid to the synergy between the two.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kate Greenaway — Artistic style
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the artistic medium and style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Is the medium appropriate? Is the style creative and distinctive? Does the style work with the subject? Is there a consistent quality of illustration throughout the book?

rubrics_metrics.name: Kate Greenaway — Format, typography and layout
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the book's typographic and layout choices as part of the artistic judgement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Is the typography (format, typeface, print size, spacing, novelty features etc.) integral or intrusive? Does the layout draw the reader in or is it distracting? How appropriate are the size and shape of the book? What use is made of covers, end-papers and title page?

rubrics_metrics.name: Kate Greenaway — Synergy of illustration and text
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess how illustration and text work together to enhance the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Are there recurring visual themes or images that enhance the reader's understanding? How well do the illustrations and text relate in terms of layout? Are the images and text consistent with each other? Do the illustrations enhance the text or are they 'pictorial upholstery' for decorative purposes only? In the case of information books, how accurate and clear are the illustrations?

rubrics_metrics.name: Kate Greenaway — Visual experience and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the overall visual experience offered by the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How well does the book either offer the reader new experiences, or reflect their pre-existing experiences? Does the book succeed in working at different levels for different readers? What are the aesthetic qualities of the book? What is the overall impact of the book on the reader?

rubrics_metrics.name: Amnesty CILIP Honour — purpose and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Two special commendations (Amnesty CILIP Honour) are awarded to an author and an illustrator — one from each shortlist — that most distinctively illuminates, communicates, or celebrates our personal rights and freedoms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Amnesty CILIP Honour is the first children’s books commendation to celebrate deep themes that are far too often ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amnesty CILIP Honour — human rights considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: In each category, the panel looks for books that celebrate values of freedom, truth, justice and fairness and contribute to a better understanding of human rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books should contribute to a better understanding of one or more human rights as stated in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and the Convention on the Rights of the Child. The best books have human rights at their core, develop empathy, and can give children the awareness and confidence to stand up and shape a better world.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability caveat for criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Not all criteria will necessarily be relevant to every title nominated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where appropriate, judges should consider and assess the listed criteria; relevance will vary by title and category.
